dev.title: Debugger does not launch Chromium if Chrome is not installed
dev.body:
Issue Type: Bug On macOS, with Chrome not installed, Chromium installed in /Applications, and the following `launch.json`: ```json { "version": "0.2.0", "configurations": [ { "type": "chrome", "request": "launch", "name": "Launch Chrome against localhost", "url": "http://localhost:3000", "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}" } ] } ``` Press F5 to start a debug session. **Expected behaviour:** Chromium launches and loads the page. **Actual behaviour:** Visual Studio Code complains that Chrome is not found. **Notes:** Chromium is Chrome without all the Google extras. It is just as capable of debugging an application. If Chrome is not installed, Visual Studio Code should fall back to Chromium. Type: Bug Submitting this issue as a continuation of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/173621, which was closed before I could gather and post results. ## Original Bug Report Glob patterns for file watcher excludes are still not working for me with the latest VSCode released last week. Local OS: Windows 11 Remote SSH host OS: centOS 7.5 I'm using a multi-root workspace through the Remote SSH extension. My multi-root workspace contains: - firmware - nvriscv - manuals Where the file tree on disk is: - /home/scratch.tcitta_gpu_1/sw/rel/firmware - /home/scratch.tcitta_gpu_1/sw/nvriscv - /home/scratch.tcitta_gpu_1/sw/resman/manuals This is a client view into a large perforce depot, so opening `.../repo` as a workspace is not an option as I am not allowed to store a .vscode directory at the upper levels of the depot. dev.title: Leave panel open when ^` shortcut returns focus to editor
dev.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

I use VS Code on macOS 10.14.6 for Python and Julia programming. Both extensions make use of an integrated interpreter/REPL. I often switch the cursor focus back and forth between the editor and the terminal using the `` ^` `` shortcut. It turns out that for this purpose, `` ^` `` and `⌘J` behave exactly the same, though I know that they are not always exactly the same. (For example, `` ^` `` will move focus from Problems/Output/Debug Console to the Terminal.)

The behavior that I find sub-optimal is that when the cursor focus is on the terminal and I hit `` ^` ``, then the focus switches to the editor _and the panel closes_. The sole purpose of the `⌘J` shortcut is to open and close the panel, so I think it would make sense if `` ^` `` did not close the panel when it switches the focus back to the editor. Then, if the user wanted to also close the panel at some later point, they can just hit `⌘J`. (Or you can use only `⌘J` if you always want the panel to close when you switch focus back to the editor.)

This modified behavior would make the `` ^` `` and `⌘J` shortcuts more decoupled from each other.

dev.title: Parenthesis, Quotation, Curly Brace, Square Brackets, Template Literal Override
dev.body:
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
Dear Developers,
I love the code editor you have introduced to us. But I have a request to fix the issue with Bracket override.
I mean when I am in Sublime Text if I type `()` and whenever my cursor is in middle of that parenthesis and if I press `)` again my cursor goes to the end of closing parenthesis. It doesn't matter how many times I press `)` when my cursor position in center of the parenthesis. Sublime Text does the magic to not put the duplicate `)`.

In Visual Studio Code if first time my cursor is in center of the parenthesis(`()`) and if I press closing bracket(`)`) the cursor goes to the end of closing bracket(`)`) which is fine. But second time if I do this again it creates another closing bracket(`)`) which I is annoying for me.

Sublime Text or Vim does not override this behaviour. So my request is to rectify this problem.

In Sublime Text
![sublime_text](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7413104/77310791-ecf5bf80-6d24-11ea-805d-96c7bff572ce.gif)

In VI improved
![vim](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7413104/77311795-cb95d300-6d26-11ea-9698-592aa02d8310.gif)

In Visual Studio Code
![vscode](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7413104/77310811-f8e18180-6d24-11ea-91bb-8e094074e06c.gif)

So, Please fix the bracket override issue in next major update. It would help my development environment.

dev.title: Can vscode be prohibited from editing official library files?
dev.body:
I have recently been using VS Code to write Python code and encountered an issue：sometimes I would open some python official library files, such as the argparse.py and torch.py. However, while editting on my own project code file, I may accidentally change the code within these official library files, causing some risk problems. Do you know of any way to prevent me from editing the official library files in VS Code (or perhaps open them in a read-only mode), allowing me to only edit my own project code files?

In fact, this functionality is available in PyCharm. For example, when I open some official library files (not my own project code) in PyCharm and try to edit these official library files, a pop-up message appears, indicating "non-project files protection" and "This file does not belong to the project". Seeing this message helps me realize my mistake and prompts me to stop my behavior. [non-project files protection](https://i.stack.imgur.com/V3ydC.png)

I tried to find the corresponding settings in vscode, or configure the related settings.json file, but unfortunately, I couldn't find it.

dev.title: add closeSidebar action
dev.body:
Add `workbench.action.closeSidebar`. It's inconsistent to have `closePanel` but not `closeSidebar`.

`toggleSidebarVisibility` exists, but that can't be used to write a macro that *closes* any open panel or sidebar: it might *open* the sidebar.

Note that this is a duplicate of https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode/issues/60241 which was opened 3 months ago then (apparently erroneously) closed as if it was a question about existing functionality when in fact it was a request for functionality that currently does not exist.

dev.title: Document/clarify whether TextDocumentContentProviders can send onDidChange only for open files
dev.body:
It's not clear to me from the API docs whether a `TextDocumentContentProviders` can selectively send `onDidChange` only if the document is open. Eg. after `didCloseTextDocument` or if a document is not in `workspace.textDocuments`, can an extension/server stop sending these messages?

My feeling is that the answer is yes (because otherwise there could be a lot of unnecessary spam), but it relies on VS Code not caching the contents of any documents that are "closed" and I'd like to be certain of this (and that it is the intention, and not only the current behaviour) before relying on that.

The docs for this field are here:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/545eb1dabec2ccca84500f47ebb740c4c7170d95/src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts#L1805

dev.title: Different behavior when reinstalling compared with uninstalling
dev.body: Type: Bug While working on developing an extension, I often need to reinstall the same version of extension through a .vsix file. However, this reinstall process is failing after taking a time of around 5 minutes. After about 5 minutes, an error message appears with the following text: Command: 'Extensions: Install from VSIX...' resulted in an error. Please restart VS Code before reinstalling ... . However, when uninstalling the same extension, the process completes much quickly and without any error messages. Similarly, reinstalling a different version of the same extension also succeeds much quickly and without any issues. Why is the reinstall process behaving differently than the uninstall process? Further, I am also unable to reproduce this issue when trying to Debug the extension, since in that case the control flow is different - with the extension being debugged directly available in the Extension Host. Moreover, I am also unable to use the Developer: Reinstall Extension command, since it is supposed to ónly work for the extensions installed through the Market Place. Searching through the list of issues, this current issue seems somewhat similar to the issue #47164. PS. After the latest update, the issue seems to have been fixed when installing locally, however, still occurs when doing a remote installation through Remote SSH. dev.title: Documents opened using `window.showTextDocument` send a delayed `didClose` event to LSP
dev.body:
Version/OS information:
```
Version: 1.85.1 (system setup)
Commit: 0ee08df0cf4527e40edc9aa28f4b5bd38bbff2b2
Date: 2023-12-13T09:49:37.021Z
Electron: 25.9.7
ElectronBuildId: 25551756
Chromium: 114.0.5735.289
Node.js: 18.15.0
V8: 11.4.183.29-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.22621
```

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Setup an LSP for some language
2. Create a file of said language
3. Open the file using the `window.showTextDocument` -> This will (correctly) send a `didOpen` request
4. Close the file -> Does not `didClose` for a while

Using the `commands` API (`commands.executeCommand("vscode.open", resourceUri, options)`) seems to work as expected (more interactive)

Related but the documentation for "vscode.open" seems to have been deleted: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/commands

Reopening the file does not resend a `didOpen` request and closing the tab does not send a `didClose` - so it must be that (for some reason) closing the file is delayed significantly. After waiting for 5 minutes, a `didClose` is actually emitted but it is very strange that using the commands API it is more predictable and interactive than the `window` API

When starting a debugging session, for example through the `[F5]` shortcut, it would be nice to have the ability to make the 'Run & Debug' tab come to focus.

If the panel it is part of is already open, the active tab should be switched to the debugging tab, and once the debugging session ends, it should switch back to the tab which was focused before. Of course, this should be a configurable feature for those who do not wish for such behaviour.

dev.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

I have a project setup where I'm using `directory-named-webpack-plugin`.

So, the imports are

```
import Header from 'components/Header';
```

Where the `components` directory contains `Header` directory which contains `Header.jsx`

Though I can configure `paths` in `jsconfig.json` for VSCode to resolve this absolute path, peeking or `Go To Definition` still does not work unless I do:

```
import Header from 'components/Header/Header';
```

Which means that VSCode import resolver looks for `index.jsx`, instead of `Header.jsx`.

Is there any existing way to tweak this behaviour?

dev.title: Missing Object.entries() in IntelliSense for JavaScript
dev.body: - VSCode Version: 1.43.2 - OS Version: macOS 10.15.4 It seems that IntelliSense is missing the [`Object.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/entries) function completely. This is weird, since being introduced with ES2017 it is pretty "old". I couldn't find any other issues on this. Then I found this statement on [Languages - JavaScript](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/javascript) > Since VS Code's JavaScript support doesn't understand ES7 constructs, features like IntelliSense might not be fully accurate. However the `String.prototype.trimStart()` and `trimEnd()` methods from ES2019 are present. So this sentence seems to be a forgotten relict from the past. I [updated the docs](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/pull/3520), but I'm still wondering why `Object.entries()` is missing from IntelliSense? (I know I could enable the TypeScript compiler for `.js` files, which would give autocomplete for `Object.entries()`, but I prefer the built-in IntelliSense since it doesn't give me red squiggly lines all over the place.) Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a `.js` file. 2. Type `Object.entries()`. 3. Watch how IntelliSense doesn't show it. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

VSCode supports configuring editor rulers, globally or for a language, using the "editor.rulers" preference. In our case we have style guides that prescribe certain line lengths for regular Python files, but they don't apply to Python cells inside notebooks, so we would like to be able to turn off rulers only in notebook editors, but not for all Python files.

dev.title: Expose webview URI
dev.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

I am writing an extension. When I invoke a command via the `editor/title` contribution, the command is called with an argument.

[Contributions](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points#menu-example)
> Note: When a command is invoked from a (context) menu, VS Code tries to infer the currently selected resource and passes that as a parameter when invoking the command.

When the editor is a webview, the argument is:
```javascript
Object
    $mid:1
    external:"webview-panel:webview-panel/webview-9dbc5868-4738-4397-81ef-a75013fcf7f9"
    path:"webview-panel/webview-9dbc5868-4738-4397-81ef-a75013fcf7f9"
    scheme:"webview-panel"
```

Now what am I supposed to do with this argument - how can I know which webview was active when my user clicked on the `editor/title` contribution?

Several options
1. Use`vscode.WebviewPanel._handle`.
In this case, it's `"9dbc5868-4738-4397-81ef-a75013fcf7f9"`.
Could work, but since it is a private field, I would rely on implementation details.
2. Constantly keep a reference to the currently active editor by listening to `onDidChangeViewState`
3. When the command is run, loop on all webviews I created, and select the one whose `active` flag is true.

Perhaps the type of the argument could also be documented

Do you recommend using `_handle` or would it be preferable for you to expose the URI?
Thanks!

dev.body:

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.76.1 (Universal)
- OS Version: macOS Ventura 13.2.1 (22D68)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a folder (name is not important);
2. Create two `.ts` files (for example `test1.ts` and `test2.ts`);
3. In `test1.ts`, create a class (for example `TestClass`) like:
```ts
// test1.ts
class TestClass {}
```
4. In `test2.ts`, create a variable (for example `test`) typed by the class and instanciate a new object like:
```ts
// test2.ts
const test: TestClass = new TestClass();
```

Current behavior:
- While having `test1.ts` closed, Intellisense doesn't detect `TestClass`, because there is no import/export in both files, as expected;
![](https://i.imgur.com/wtu13zp.png)
- While having `test1.ts` opened, Intellisense detect `TestClass`, even if there is no import/export in both files. The link is broken when an export statement is defined in `test1.ts` or, in case of a class, an argument is required into the constructor;
![](https://i.imgur.com/29bC0C7.png)
![](https://i.imgur.com/yO5x7fc.png)
![](https://i.imgur.com/TVDPKhR.png)
This behavior is the same with other declarations (interface, type for example).

Expected behavior:
- Intellisense should not be able to detect `TestClass` in any case, as there is no import nor export.
- Intellisense should be able to detect `TestClass` in `test2.ts` only if `TestClass` is exported in `test1.ts` and imported as `TestClass` in `test2.ts`;

Tried actions to solve the issue:
- Clean all VScode installation as described on [VScode documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/uninstall#_clean-uninstall) and reinstall it;
- Run it without extensions by running `code --disable-extensions`;

dev.title: please add a better way to force focus back to the editor
dev.body: Issue Type: Feature Request One problem with VSCode and screen readers is this: there seems to be no quick way to return focus to the editor after switching views. 1. Open a few files. Be sure you're in the editor for a file. 2. Press ctrl-shift-f to do a global search. 3. Try to get out of that and back to your editor. Since global find is a view, and the editor isn't a view but is always visible (I think), there's no keystroke/command to put you back in the editor. I usually press ctrl-1, but if you use multiple groups, you have to know which group you want. Ctrl-k, e is the other option, but that puts you in a list, not straight back into the most recent editor. It seems like there should be an easy way to get out of global search, debug, and the other views and back into the active editor. Yes, ctrl-k then e will bring up a list of editors with the most recent at the top, but you then have to press enter. Ctrl-{1-0} will work, but you have to know which group you want. The solutions I can come up with: 1. Offer a setting that allows the user to choose the behavior of ctrl-k, e. Either go to the most recent editor, or offer the list as happens now. Remapping this command and changing the setting would thus offer a single keystroke method for getting into the editor. 2. Offer a new command, and clarify the existing one so it is obvious that it will go to a list and not directly back to the editor. Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create an extension
2. In the plugin code try to send an POST https request to a server with expired certificate like:

    const response = await fetch('https://some-expired-cert-server.com/request', {
      method: 'POST', 
      body: {},
      headers, 
      agent: agent}
    );
Where agent is like:
const agent = https.Agent({rejectUnauthorized: false};

You will get an exception "request to https://some-expired-cert-server.com/request failed, reason: certificate has expired" 

Expected behavior is that no exception should happen when rejectUnauthorized: false.
Possible workaround in the code: process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '0'; but it's not advisable.

dev.title: Allow the `provideCompletionItems` method to exist with `triggerCharacters` parameters as optional instead of being mandatory.
dev.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Allow the `provideCompletionItems` method to exist with `triggerCharacters` parameters as optional. In that case, alphanumerical characters are also triggers for code completion by default.

I'm not sure whether this is a bug or a feature. I'll treat it as a feature for now. Anyway, I'm currently using the `provideCompletionItems` method for a VS Code Extension which seems to require at least 1 non-alphanumerical character as a trigger. This is the `triggerCharacters` parameter of that same method. However, that doesn't align with how VS Code works out-of-the-box with code completions from IntelliSense. At least not in a JavaScript file. For example, as soon as you type the character "d" in a JavaScript file, out-of-the-box code completions are already suggested (for example, "debugger"). On the other hand, if I write my own VS Code Extension and I want my own code completions, it seems that I must specify a non-alphanumerical character as a trigger (for example, "/"). What I'd like to do is to allow completions without having to rely on a trigger character that isn't alphanumerical. For example, if I type the letter "a" within a single-line comment then my VS Code Extension can retrieve a list of identifiers in that file that start with the letter "a".

Thank you.

dev.title: How to update a single child node from a list of hundreds of child nodes under a TreeItem parent
dev.body:
I have an Explorer Treeview and a parent in the tree can have hundreds of child nodes.  Each child node then has right click options to perform specific tasks.  
A right click option can change the state of the child node and so I need to refresh that child node in order toe re-establish the current state and refresh the right click options.
Currently, I am having to perform a refresh on the parent node which is then triggerts onDidChangeTreeData  which then in turn triggers getChildren to go  rebuild that entire child structure below the parent. This all works but it is very  inefficient and takes time to go through and rebuild as there can be hundreds of child nodes and each is refreshed by issuing a REST api to another platform.

 I can find no documentation on how I can get access to just the specific child node from the array of child nodes that was originally created in getChildren too allow me to update just that single child entry..
 
 Is there the ability to update a single child node ? I have not found any example of suggestions in this area.
 
 Same question for deleting one single child node ?? Without having to rebuild the entire parent structure? 
 
 Thanks

dev.title: It is not possible to create a snippet that outputs multiple backslashes
dev.body:
The problem here is well understood and has been reported multiple times:
#32020
#59668
#33933
#47529

For background - textmate backslash handling combined with JSON backslash handling results in multiple backslashes being elided into one. This means you can't create snippets that output multiple backslashes. In my case that's an issue because that's the syntax for default args in elixir.

These issues have all been closed as dupes of  (as far as I can tell) #32020. That has been closed as #25661 would sort it out, except that #25661 has also been closed as out-of-scope.

This leaves us with no way to write these snippets, no issue tracking fixing that problem and no workaround in the meantime.

My proposal to fix this would be to add an option to the snippet syntax. If the property `"textmate_backslashes": false` was set on the snippet object, then textmate backslash elision wouldn't happen and `\\\\` in JSON would output as `\\`.
This would add the functionality, while not breaking anyone's existing snippets.

dev.title: Restart specific debugger using command
dev.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Hi there.

A bit of background for the setup: I'm working with an Electron application, which requires two different debugging configurations - one for the main process, one for the renderer. I set up my `launch.json` so that the *chrome attach* automatically runs when the *node launch* is done starting (the same could also be achieved through a compound configuration).

But this setup has a major inconvenience: Whenever a task, extension or the user runs the "Debug: Restart" command, it restarts the configuration that is currently selected in the debugging widget (the one with the pause, continue and step buttons) or the "Debug Console" tab. By default, that's the main process launcher. Unfortunately, in 99% of cases the intended behavior is to restart the renderer, not the launcher, which means that the wrong debugger is restarted if the user doesn't pay attention to the currently selected one.

What I want to do is to configure a preferred debugger that will be restarted when the `workbench.action.debug.restart` command is invoked.
- One possible solution would be to add a launch.json option for runtime priority so that the renderer can be selected, e.g. through a new *presentation* property (or by respecting the existing *order* option).
- Another solution would be a parameter for the command, although I am not sure how that would interact with calling it from a task (using the `${command:<command>}` syntax).

I am, of course, open for alternative solutions.

I'm trying to debug something. I've manually placed a breakpoint in JS code. Smart step skips over it and breaks in some completely unrelated code that it decided was more relevant. Trying to step into the method from the caller or step out from a method that it calls just leads to it getting skipped again.

Since this feature got released, I don't think I've ever gotten joy from using it, but I have had near constant pain from issues like this.

My ask is to provide a way to disable it permanently in the normal user settings.

Using [Terminal profiles](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_55#_terminal-profiles) introduced in `1.55` (via #45444) I tried to use system variables as part of `path` and `args` values but w/o success.

Example for `path`:
* this one **works**:
```
"terminal.integrated.profiles.windows": {
        "Yet Another PowerShell": {
            "path": "c:\\Users\\Piotr\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\pwsh.exe"
        }
}
```
* this one **does not work** - it's not even listed on the list of available profiles:
```
"terminal.integrated.profiles.windows": {
        "Yet Another PowerShell": {
            "path": "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\pwsh.exe"
        },
}
```

Same thing is observed if variable is used as part of value of `args`. Following configuration:
```
"terminal.integrated.profiles.windows": {
        "Yet Another PowerShell": {
            "path": "c:\\Users\\Piotr\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\pwsh.exe"
            "args": [
                "-noexit",
                "-file",
                "%APPDATA%\\PowerShell\\oh-my-posh.ps1"
            ]
        }
}
```
fails with error:

```

dev.title: launch.json configuration generated command can't be parsed by external program because multi-word argument has single quotes around it
dev.body:
In debug configurations (launch.json), when arguments are multi-word such as "--config someArg someVal", they are parsed into '--config someArg someVal' and appended to the final run command (including single-quotes). Is there a way to prevent this behaviour and keep them as they are?

After running the config below I get the following command:
`'C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe' --debug-brk=32795 --nolazy node_modules\jasmine-node\lib\jasmine-node\cli.js --color --verbose --captureExceptions '--config someArg someVal' someDir`

jasmine-node does not recognize its format and displays the help text, so the debug output is:

```
USAGE: jasmine-node [--color|--noColor] [--verbose] [--coffee] directory
Options:
...
--config NAME VALUE- set a global variable in process.env
...
```

If I remove the --config arg the debug session starts (and an exception is thrown since the env arg is missing).

Now, if I remove the single quotes around '--config someVar someVal' and then run the command in a terminal, the program runs.

It seems jasmine is unable to parse the argument when it's around single quotes, and I can't use the VSCode debugger. Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks!

dev.title: Schema `"defaultSnippets"` backslash escapes don't work
dev.body:
I am unable to backslash escape snippet syntax
I wanted to input the literal characters `$` and `1`, but instead I get a tabstop
Workaround is to use [Variable Transforms](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/userdefinedsnippets#_variable-transforms)
`$${github_com_microsoft_vscode_issues_200424///}1`

https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/userdefinedsnippets#_grammar
> With `\` (backslash), you can escape `$`, `}`, and `\`.

Create a valid schema file with the contents
```json
"defaultSnippets": [
	{
		"label": "vscode bug",
		"body": [
			"^ $1 $2",
			"\\^ \\${1:1} $\\2",
			"\\\\^ \\\\$1 $\\\\2",
			"\\\\\\^ \\\\\\$1 $\\\\\\2",
			"\\\\\\\\^ \\\\\\\\$1 $\\\\\\\\2"
		]
	}
]
```
Assign the schema to a json file and press `ctrl+space` to bring up `completions`
Trigger the `vscode bug` snippet and watch how the snippet syntax was escaped incorrectly, causing many json errors.

![image](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/33529441/43e178dc-0c79-45f7-b788-bfa3d580baba)
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/33529441/c550f6fd-10b3-4a90-aacc-5b92975156b5)
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/33529441/b8afc2f9-ae66-4299-b68a-f1c13084a210)
also notice how having `^` at the beginning of a string removes the double quotes.
This can be considered a feature, but not being able to escape it is still a bug

The same is also for `"$schema"`
Workaround was `"$${github_com_microsoft_vscode_issues_200424///}schema"`

Save the file Notice how the whitespaces at end of file are removed on save. ![image](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/808610/43c41c62-865b-4059-bc82-99dcf7c7a9cd) 5. Undo the cleanup (`ctrl+z`) 6. File > Preferences > Settings 7. Search for `formatOnSave` 8. Click it to set, then unset (so it's not "reset", but explicitly "false" in config file) Notice at this point, there shouldn't be an option to choose between **User** and **Workspace** scopes because the project was not started by opening a folder. Switching to a scenario where a folder is opened makes no difference, thus disabling the setting to user/workspace scopes makes no difference either. 9. Repeat (4), after ensuring (5) added back the whitespace characters to the end of the sentence, or just adding back the whitespace characters to the end of the line. The result is the same as (4), the file is cleaned from the trailing whitespaces regardless of `editor.formatOnSave` being `false`. This has been reported a long time ago in https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode/issues/53988, and also has a relevant upvote in https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61827206/vscode-disable-all-auto-formatting-on-save The accepted solution in the thread (replace the `ctrl+s` hotkey to "save without formatting") is the only effective workaround, and by the answer there, the user is in macos, so this seems to be a cross-platform issue haunting it for a long time. It does not matter whether user or workspace setting for `file.formatOnSave` is reset, enabled or disabled for either user or workspace scopes. There are other issues reported where the original reporter didn't confirm it was caused by an extension, like #29335, Besides, to reproduce the scenario above, I simply opened VSCode, then created a new file and saved it in a new, empty directory. ### Context This is actually a nice feature when set up properly, but it can become a bother when VSCode can't talk properly with version control system in a (legacy) project with lots of formatting issues (or different formatting tastes), thus polluting considerably a file change, say, when there's a small fix. This would mean, for instance, even with `editor.formatOnSaveMode` as `modifications`, it would format the whole file every time it is saved, literally making a commit to the file useless to the purpose of identifying the actual changes in the file. heldout.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Hi! While setting up VSCode, I found out it supports only Node `v16>` and `<v17` because it apparently depends on package `@azure/[redacted]`.

Reading on [@azure/msal-node](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@azure/msal-node),
> MSAL Node enables applications to authenticate users using [Azure AD](https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/develop/v2-overview) work and school accounts (AAD), Microsoft personal accounts (MSA) and social identity providers like Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft accounts, etc. through [Azure AD B2C](https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory-b2c/active-directory-b2c-overview#identity-providers) service

It seems package `@azure/identity` version `^2.0.4` is at fault. `build/package.json`.

Why is this in build package.json? This really shouldn't be a core vscode thing. sure, you can bundle it in a builtin extension, but right in the VSCode base code? Why? To overcome a self-imposed limitation (extensions can't put new actions in the lower part of the activity bar, as far as I know)?

This is not a nerdy linux open source guy thing, `@azure/identity` requires an Azure subscription. Is this really the way in an open source product?

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: YES

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.85.1
- OS Version: OSX 14.1.2

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Set your settings as below.
2. Open any markdown file.

```json
{
  "editor.wordWrapColumn": 60,
  "editor.wordWrap": "bounded",
}
```

Markdown wraps to the editor width properly, but not to the wrap column. It makes editing markdown files a pain to work with. It doesn't happen with plain text. Nor does it happen with MDX files when using the MDX extension.

heldout.title: Provide setting to disable baseUrl style imports
heldout.body:
If a `baseUrl` is set vscode uses `src/foo.js`. In NestJS `baseUrl` is set so that tsconfig-paths works. The author [discourages](https://github.com/nestjs/typescript-starter/issues/74#issuecomment-464698726) the `src/` imports, but cannot remove `baseUrl` because that would disable `paths`.

Please provide an option to disable the `baseUrl` imports so only relative and paths imports are used.

heldout.title: Terminal: Ability to pass Page Up / Page Down and possibly other keys directly to the terminal
heldout.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Page Down (Linux) and Fn + Down (Mac) performs `workbench.action.terminal.scrollDown` action by default. This is great and it should stay like that.

However, there's situations when we need to pass the "Page Down" key to the underlying terminal. For example, when looking at a long `git diff` that uses a pager. Because Page Down key is hijacked by VSCode, there's no way to pass it to the underlying shell session when using the Terminal.

General idea: Please us to pass the keys that are normally hijacked by VSCode to the underlying shell session under certain conditions.

Specific ideas:

- Proposal 1: When Ctrl+Shift+[key] (Linux) or Fn+Shift+[key] (Mac) are pressed, pass [key] directly to the session. The most feasible solution for that would be a new keybinding, e.g. `workbench.action.terminal.passKeyCombination` = `Ctrl+Shift`.
- Proposal 2: Introduce keystroke action for each key, e.g. `workbench.action.terminal.sendKey.pageDown`, `...pageUp`, and so on, and allow us to bind any key (e.g. Ctrl+Shift+PageDown) to that action. Some reasonable defaults for Linux and Mac should be provided.

heldout.title: Insecure default location for customization files
heldout.body:
When creating a workspace, the *default* location for customized json files, such as tasks.json, launch.json, etc, should *not* be in the project source directory.

This is *BAD* default location, since a full refresh by a revision control system will wipe all those files out.

The current default behavior is just plain wrong.  The default location should be in the users profile area ($USER)/.vscode or similar

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
When using extensions like the Python extension, there is a button to execute open files. However, at least in case of the Python extension there is no default keyboard shortcut for this often used action.

I created an issue about this for the extension (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/issues/16340) and a reason for them to not provide a default shortcut is to avoid interference with shortcuts from VS Code or other extensions.

Since I assume that there are multiple extensions offering something like the run button of the Python extension, it might help to have a global (and default) shortcut for this.

heldout.title: git: warn before commiting if there are pending commits to download/pull
heldout.body:
The sync status on the bottom bar is quite nice, but way too small and, now that we are migrating one of our development teams to Visual Studio Code + git (they used a different IDE and source control system before), we are finding that our repositories are full of "automerges", due to the fact that it is very easy to commit some changes before realising that someone else had also made changes to the project.

It would be nice if there was an option, say *fetchBeforeCommit* or something similar, that run the "git fetch" command before confirming the commit and, if there are commits that have not been pulled yet, ask the user whether they want to continue commiting (and thus requiere a merge), or cancel the action.

heldout.title: Small user snippet issue using single quotes
heldout.body:
I noticed this issue happening after the February update (I think). I'll try to explain this the best way I can. When I want to insert single quotes ' ', I press the single quote button once and 2 quotes appear. The cursor/pointer is inbetween those 2 quotes. After pressing backspace/delete, both of the quotes dissapear again. This is expected behaviour. 

Now, I use a snippet to print a console.log line, like so: 
```
"Print to console": {
    "prefix": "cl",
    "body": [
	"console.log('$1');",
	"$2"
    ],
    "description": "Log output to console"
}
```

My cursor starts at `$1`, so in between the quotes. When I want to remove both quotes by pressing backspace once, only the left one deletes. This used to work like mentioned above, where both single quotes would be removed. 

When I try to manually write `console.log('');`, go in between the quotes and press delete, both of the quotes go away, which is expected behaviour. So I guess the issue lies in the snippet quotes.


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21953348/113693148-96101d80-96ce-11eb-8a92-15739c6f36a4.mov

As you see, when using the snippet and pressing delete afterwards, only the left one removes, instead of both. After manually typing quotes, they both delete when pressing backspace.

heldout.title: Support multiple saved sessions
heldout.body:
When I close vscode with unsaved files it saves the session and exits without prompting to save. This is a great feature. However, if I have 2 instances of vscode open and I attempt to close one of them it prompts me to save. I'd like it to simply save the session like it does for the single instance case.

The same issue existing when running a single instance and attempting to switch to another folder or workspace.

It seems vscode nearly supports this capability already. Each folder or workspace I open remembers which editors are open, as long as they don't have unsaved changes. It's unclear why this doesn't extend to editors with unsaved changes, but I very much wish it did.

heldout.title: Be able to see if two files/functions are connected at all
heldout.body:
Often I need to know if this function is being called by code whether it's parent or child. Only way for me to is trace all imports and see they invoke anything if not then trace their imports. Similarly, see all references and see if THEY call the function in question, if not see if any of their children do. 

Reason I've to check children and parents is because how convoluted react code becomes. Data is being passed 8 levels down and then 5 levels further. Sometimes you need a certain piece of data and you wonder if xyz is already being called in some manner or not. 

Extra bonus: if works react context and redux.
